09 — Overview

How skills work, and why the description is separate from the body. Read this before you write code.

One file, two audiences

A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md:

skills/deploy/SKILL.md
---
name: deploy
description: Deploy the app to a region.
---
Check the tests pass, then deploy to $0 in $1.
Report the deployed version. Full request: $ARGUMENTS

The file has two audiences and they read different parts:

PartAudienceWhen it is sent
name, descriptionthe model, every requestalways
bodythe model, only when invokedon /deploy
the whole fileyou, and the agent's loadernever verbatim

That split is the feature. A project with fifty skills pays fifty lines on every request, not fifty documents. The alternative, sending every body, is the tool schema problem from chapter 07 with a different name.

Invocation is text substitution, not a tool call

A tool call is the model's decision. A skill invocation is the person's: they type /deploy staging, and the agent expands it before the model sees anything.

  typed:   /deploy staging eu-west
  sent:    Check the tests pass, then deploy to staging in eu-west.
           Report the deployed version. Full request: staging eu-west

Three consequences:

  1. The model never sees the shorthand. It sees instructions, which is what it

can act on.

  1. Expansion happens before the session records the turn. A resumed run replays

what was sent, not the shorthand.

  1. An unknown name is passed through. Deleting the person's text because of a

typo is worse than sending a slash command the model ignores.

Placeholders

Two forms, often in one body:

PlaceholderReplaced with
$ARGUMENTSeverything after the skill name, as one string
$0, $1, $2one whitespace-separated word, by position
$9 with no argumentthe empty string

Replace $ARGUMENTS first. Both forms start with $, and a positional pass that runs first can corrupt the longer token.

  args:  staging eu-west
  "Deploy to $0 in $1. Full: $ARGUMENTS"
  → "Deploy to staging in eu-west. Full: staging eu-west"

Arguments are split on whitespace. Quoting inside an argument is not handled, and the overview says so rather than implying otherwise.

Stacking

One prompt can name several skills. Arguments run from the skill name to the next slash command:

  "/review /deploy production eu-west"

  review  → arguments: ""                    (nothing before the next command)
  deploy  → arguments: "production eu-west"

Expansion walks left to right and preserves order, because the order is the instruction. "Review, then deploy" and "deploy, then review" are different jobs.

The catalogue is a Contributor

Chapter 05 built the seam for exactly this:

system, err := agent.BuildSystemPrompt(ctx, agent.BasePrompt,
	&agent.AgentsFile{Root: root},
	catalog,                  // ← skills, added in this chapter
)

Catalog.Contribute renders the list. The prompt builder did not change. The loop did not change. That is the third chapter in a row where a feature arrived without touching either.

Why the frontmatter is not YAML

name: and description: on their own lines between --- fences is enough for this feature and needs no dependency. A real SKILL.md format often uses YAML with lists and nesting; that is a dependency and a specification, and neither is the lesson here.

The rule this chapter does keep from real formats: a file that cannot be parsed is skipped, not fatal. One malformed skill must not stop the agent from starting.

What this chapter does not do

  • No scripts. A skill is instructions, not a bundled program.
  • No named arguments. Only $ARGUMENTS and positional.
  • No model-chosen invocation. The person types the slash command. Letting the

model choose from the catalogue is a tool-calling problem, and chapter 04 already covered the mechanism.

  • No skill events. A terminal UI would want one; the event stream does not have

it yet.

Where the real implementations go further

ConcernImplementation
Progressive disclosurepi skills: description first, body on demand
Skill directories with scriptsCodeCrafters "run a script bundled with a skill"
Model-chosen skillsthe catalogue as a tool, not a prompt section
Frontmatter with lists and defaultsYAML parsing

The first row is this chapter. The second is a natural extension for a learner who wants to keep going, and it is listed in "where next".

Self-check

  1. Which part of a skill is sent on every request, and why is the other part not?

(One file, two audiences)

  1. Who decides to invoke a skill: the model or the person? *(Invocation is text

substitution, not a tool call)*

  1. Why is $ARGUMENTS replaced before $0? (Placeholders)
  2. How are arguments delimited when two skills share a prompt? (Stacking)
  3. What happens to a skill file that has no frontmatter, and why is that the right

choice? (Why the frontmatter is not YAML)
